title: Temple Architecture: Nagara, Dravida, Vesara

cards.b: Temples are the best-preserved record of Indian kings, faith and craft. UPSC asks for style features, dynasties and examples, often with a UNESCO angle.

Garbhagriha (sanctum), mandapa (hall), shikhara or vimana (tower), antarala (vestibule), amalaka (ribbed disc on Nagara tower), kalasha (finial). Early Gupta temples (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon brick temple) set the pattern. The three broad styles are described in the Vastu texts: Nagara (north), Dravida (south), Vesara (Deccan mix).

Found from the Himalayas to the Vindhyas. Features: a curved shikhara (rekha-deula or latina type), temple on a raised platform, no boundary wall or large gateway. Sub-schools: Odisha (Lingaraja, Bhubaneswar; Konark Sun Temple; Jagannath, Puri; deul and jagamohana), Khajuraho (Chandela, Kandariya Mahadeva, c. 1000 CE; panchayatana plan), Solanki (Modhera Sun Temple, Gujarat, 1026), Dilwara Jain temples (Mount Abu).

The tower is a stepped pyramid, vimana, with a rectangular compound wall and a large gopuram at the gateway. A water tank and pillared halls are common. Dynasties: Pallavas (Mahabalipuram Shore Temple, Kanchi Kailasanatha), Cholas (Brihadisvara, Thanjavur, built by Rajaraja I about 1010 CE; Gangaikonda Cholapuram; Airavatesvara, Darasuram), Pandyas and Nayakas (Madurai Meenakshi, large gopurams).

Vesara is the mixed style of the Deccan. Chalukyas of Badami and Aihole (Durga temple, Virupaksha at Pattadakal), Rashtrakutas (Kailasa at Ellora, carved from one rock under Krishna I), Hoysalas (Belur, Halebid, Somnathpur; star-shaped plan on a platform, soapstone, called jagati). Others: Kashmir (Martand Sun Temple, Karkota), Himachal (wooden temples), Kerala (sloping roofs), Assam (Kamakhya).

Barabar caves (Mauryan, polished). Kanheri, Karle. Elephanta (Shiva, Maharashtra). The Kailasa temple at Ellora is carved top down from a single rock. Pallava monolithic rathas at Mahabalipuram (Narasimhavarman I Mamalla). Ajanta and Ellora combine Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves.

The Nagara-Dravida-Vesara scheme is helpful but not sharp: Odisha and Khajuraho differ from each other, and the Deccan mixed both. Scholars such as Adam Hardy speak of a “Karnata Dravida” tradition. Still, for exams, learn the three types and exceptions.

Great Living Chola Temples (Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Darasuram), Khajuraho, Konark, Mahabalipuram, Pattadakal, Hampi and the Hoysala temples are UNESCO World Heritage sites (the Hoysala group was added in 2023). The Ram temple at Ayodhya (consecrated January 2024) is built in the Nagara style. Temple economy and the HR&CE laws in states raise legal debates.

• “Distinguish between Nagara and Dravida architecture.” Use a two-column table.
  • “Chola temple architecture was a mirror of imperial power.”
  • Prelims tip: gopuram = Dravida; shikhara with amalaka = Nagara; star plan = Hoysala; Kailasa at Ellora = Rashtrakuta.
